title: Ukulele strum-along
summary: The 'ukulele is a small four-string guitar that took its Hawaiian form in the 1880s from small guitars brought by Portuguese settlers. Its re-entrant tuning gives a bright, chiming strum that suits singing along.
howToPlay: The four strings are on the top row and four chord strums on the lower row.
Notes travel toward a line at the bottom; strike the lane just as a note arrives.
In the first song, strum the chord named in each bar with a down, a down-up and an up-down-up.
Then pick the strings one by one in the arpeggio, and finish with the short chop strum.
rules: The strings are tuned G, C, E, A with the G above the C, a re-entrant tuning.
A stroke within a hair of the note is perfect, a near one is good, and a missed one scores nothing.
An extra stroke while a song is running costs a few points.
Each song plays twice; three stars need roughly nine notes in ten on time.
A chord lane is one sounded note at the chord's root; strum direction is not judged.
heritageNote: The 'ukulele grew from small guitars of Madeira that reached Hawaii in 1879. It became a staple of island music and is now played in schools, bands and living rooms around the world.
